### N-Channel Enhancement-Type MOSFET (E-MOSFET)

#### Construction:
* It consists of a p-type substrate into which two heavily doped n-type regions (source and drain) are diffused.
* Unlike the depletion MOSFET, **there is no physical channel** between the source and drain; the p-substrate extends all the way to the $	ext{SiO}_2$ insulating layer under the gate.
* A metal gate electrode is placed on top of a silicon dioxide ($	ext{SiO}_2$) insulating layer.

#### Working Operation:
* When $V_{GS} = 0 	ext{ V}$ and a positive drain-to-source voltage ($V_{DS}$) is applied, the two back-to-back p-n junctions prevent current flow; hence, $I_D 	o 0$.
* When a positive gate voltage greater than the threshold voltage ($V_{GS} > V_{TN}$) is applied, it repels positive holes in the p-substrate away from the gate region and attracts minority carrier electrons upward.
* These accumulated electrons form an induced n-channel connecting the source and drain, allowing drain current ($I_D$) to flow. Increasing $V_{GS}$ enhances (widens) the channel, increasing $I_D$.

#### Characteristics (Description):
* **Drain Characteristics ($I_D$ vs $V_{DS}$):** Shows distinct triode (ohmic) and saturation regions for different values of $V_{GS} > V_{TN}$. Current remains nearly constant in the saturation region once $V_{DS} \ge V_{GS} - V_{TN}$.
* **Transfer Characteristics ($I_D$ vs $V_{GS}$):** A square-law relationship curve starting only after $V_{GS}$ exceeds the threshold voltage $V_{TN}$ ($I_D = K(V_{GS} - V_{TN})^2$).
proTip: Emphasize that the E-MOSFET has *no physical channel* at $V_{GS}=0$, requiring a threshold voltage ($V_{TN}$) to *enhance* (induce) the channel.
